title: Understanding a Basic Contract
text:
A contract is a legally binding agreement between two or more parties. For a contract to be valid, the parties must have the capacity to enter into it, there must be a clear offer and acceptance, and each party must provide something of value, known as consideration. Courts generally expect the terms of a contract to be written in plain language so that everyone understands their obligations. If one party breaks the terms, the other party may be entitled to compensation.

Many contracts include a clause that limits liability, which sets a maximum amount one party can be required to pay. Another common clause is the termination clause, which explains how either party can end the agreement early. Some contracts also specify which country's laws will govern any dispute. Because these provisions can be complicated, many people ask a lawyer to review a document before they sign it.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must each party provide?
options: Something of value, known as consideration
A signed copy of the law

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what does a termination clause explain?
options: How much money a party must pay
How either party can end the agreement early

questions.text: Why might a person ask a lawyer to review a contract before signing it?
options: Because lawyers write all contracts for free
Because the court requires it every time
Because the provisions can be complicated

questions.text: What can be inferred about a clause that limits liability?
options: It removes the need for any written terms
It guarantees that a party will receive payment
It protects a party from paying an unlimited amount
It means the contract cannot be ended

paragraph_translations: Un contrato es un acuerdo legalmente vinculante entre dos o más partes. Para que un contrato sea válido, las partes deben tener capacidad para celebrarlo, debe haber una oferta y una aceptación claras, y cada parte debe aportar algo de valor, conocido como contraprestación. Los tribunales generalmente esperan que los términos de un contrato se redacten en un lenguaje sencillo para que todos entiendan sus obligaciones. Si una parte incumple los términos, la otra parte puede tener derecho a una compensación.

Muchos contratos incluyen una cláusula que limita la responsabilidad, la cual establece una cantidad máxima que una parte puede estar obligada a pagar. Otra cláusula común es la de rescisión, que explica cómo cualquiera de las partes puede poner fin al acuerdo antes de tiempo. Algunos contratos también especifican qué leyes de qué país regirán cualquier disputa. Como estas disposiciones pueden ser complicadas, muchas personas piden a un abogado que revise un documento antes de firmarlo.
